title: Whole Globular Chambers and Rimmed Aperture Foraminifer
description: One wholly newly authored enlarged low-trochospiral foraminifer-inspired exterior test. Four smaller complete early chambers lead into four embracing globular chambers in the final whorl, with actual depressed sutural boundaries and an open umbilical region. The final chamber has a full inner wall and a genuinely open elliptical primary aperture with an integral finite lip, not a painted dark spot or separate decorative ring. All chamber centres, profiles, broad roots, rim and cavity topology are new; no nautilus shell, tentacle, planar fossil section, stone matrix, radiolarian lattice or pollen geometry is copied. Eight closed editable components, three opaque quiet limestone PBR roles, one complete exterior teaching prop and zero scenes. The specimen is deliberately displayed with its umbilical face upward; the smaller early chambers form the opposite low spiral side. Shallow surface pits are coarse relief only: microscopic wall perforations, spines, early internal chambers and connecting foramina are not modelled. This is a generic regularized exterior, not a named species, exact chamber count, measured specimen, living cytoplasm, fossil reconstruction, material microstructure, buoyancy, climate proxy, physical or biological simulation. Arbitrary roughly twelve-centimetre display scale. A small lower early-chamber datum is only for display, not natural orientation or stability. No labels, textures, transparency, rig, animation or interaction.
